\begin{abstract}
Adapting a vision--language model (VLM) to a new Vietnamese Visual Question Answering
(VQA) benchmark usually means fine-tuning it on many high-resolution image tiles or
training a new architecture. We propose \textbf{ViBridge-VQA}, which improves the
Vietnamese VLM Vintern-1B while keeping its vision encoder, its projector and its
language decoder frozen. ViBridge-VQA feeds the decoder two complementary kinds of
visual tokens from a single image view: \emph{global} tokens, produced by a small
trainable bridge from the \texttt{[CLS]} vector that Vintern-1B discards, and
\emph{local} tokens, produced by Vintern-1B's own pre-aligned projector and pooled to a
chosen budget. Only the global bridge is trained (1.35\% of the parameters). We select
the token budget as the knee of the accuracy--cost Pareto front, which falls on the
same configuration (14 global and 36 local tokens) for all eight metrics on both
validation and test, with cost measured in tokens or in inference time. On AutoViVQA,
ViBridge-VQA raises the F1 of Vintern-1B from 17.6 to 54.6 and outperforms the
officially fine-tuned Vintern-1B on seven of eight metrics while passing 50 instead of
up to 1{,}792 visual tokens; with all 144 local tokens it outperforms it on all eight
(F1 +2.3, CIDEr +43.9). Local tokens matter far more than global ones and help most on
perception-heavy questions, and without any decoder adaptation the model surpasses our
best decoder-LoRA model.

\keywords{Vietnamese Visual Question Answering \and Vision--Language Models \and
Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning \and Low-Rank Adaptation \and Generative VQA}
\end{abstract}
